key_insight: Polynomial reduced-order models paired with quantum transport preserve nonlinear flow dynamics while making per-step rotation counts polylogarithmic in grid resolution at fixed model dimension and drift degree.
engineering_relevance: Choosing reduced-model polynomial degree to balance accuracy and circuit cost offers a design lever for early fault-tolerant quantum flow simulation.
method: Fit polynomial reduced-order models using sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics.
Implement Koopman–von Neumann transport with Walsh-synthesized quantum circuits.
Estimate end-to-end runtime and physical-qubit requirements using surface-code resources.
evidence_signal: For a cylinder wake approaching saturation, the study estimates 1.62 hours on about 560,000 physical qubits for 1% relative RMS field error against the radial model, and demonstrates nonlinear radial transport on IBM hardware with reference-circuit noise mitigation.
watch_item: The fault-tolerant runtimes are estimates, and the reported 1% error is measured against a reduced radial model rather than a full-flow reference.
paper_title: Nonlinearity-preserving quantum simulation of flows in the early fault-tolerant regime
